pattern_tunnel_machine.name: Pattern Tunnel Machine
pattern_tunnel_machine.description: A subway-tiled walkway tunnel that paints itself tile by tile (floor then walls then ceiling), driven by a pattern-maker console at the mouth. The console's GROUP / MOTIF / PALETTE / SPEED sliders re-skin the whole tube through any of the 17 wallpaper symmetry groups; touching a control surges the fill faster. Same WallpaperGroups engine as pattern_studio_plate.

parameters.fill_speed: rings per second the tunnel paints

pattern_tunnel_machine.qfep_connection: f_order: the tunnel that paints itself — a subway-tiled walkway laid tile by tile from a pattern console at its mouth; ornament as a running program you can walk into while it executes.

CaveGenerator.name: CaveGenerator
CaveGenerator.qfep_connection: Majority rule run five generations over random rock: solid survives with four neighbours, void turns solid at five. Only the rock gets instanced — the cave is never built, it is everywhere the multimesh declined to place a cube.

GeneticProgramming.description: Watch 3D creatures evolve generation by generation toward a fitness goal no individual understands. Population grid displays organisms with fitness labels. Auto-evolve ticks on a timer or step manually. Creatures converge on similar body plans despite random initialization — convergent evolution from pure math. Evolution does not design — it accumulates accidents that happen to survive.
GeneticProgramming.qfep_connection: phi-dE — the rate of evolutionary change. Each generation is a dE step. Fitness is the selection pressure (phi) that amplifies some mutations and kills others. Lambda emerges as the mutation rate: too low and evolution stalls, too high and it melts.
GeneticProgramming.gamwell_reference: Constraint satisfaction, evolutionary computation, genetic algorithms
GeneticProgramming.capacity: WATCH evolution accumulate accidents that happen to survive — design without a designer
interactions: observe fitness labels on population grid
GeneticProgramming.name: GeneticProgramming

GyroidDemo.name: GyroidDemo
GyroidDemo.qfep_connection: A surface nobody modeled: the gyroid's implicit equation marched into triangles by a compute shader, dividing space into two labyrinths that never touch. If the GPU declines, the fallback is a sphere — an admission that without the equation there is no shape to fall back on.

SierpinskiPyramid.description: pyramid(depth) = 5 * pyramid(depth-1) — top + four corners, recursively
SierpinskiPyramid.name: SierpinskiPyramid

WFC3DGenerator.name: WWFC3DGeneratorr
WFC3DGenerator.qfep_connection: Socket-grammar collapse where the Rainbow_Dance_Floor's weight of 6 outbids the plain Floor's 5: the tile library is a constitution, and one number legislates what kind of room is statistically likely to exist. Joy doesn't emerge from constraint propagation — it has to be given majority weight before the dice are allowed to find it.

WFCCav.name: WFCCav
WFCCav.qfep_connection: Twenty hand-written tile types — tunnels, corners, T-junctions, stalactites — each with a dictionary declaring which directions it will speak to. The 'organic' cavern is adjacency bureaucracy: nature specified as a plumbing catalogue, then rolled until the paperwork is consistent.

WFCSculptureGenerator.name: WFCSculptureGenerator
WFCSculptureGenerator.qfep_connection: Every cell knows its distance to center and to surface before any collapse, and the voxel weights bend to that geography — so the 'discovered' sculpture is a CORE_SOLID-to-SURFACE_POROUS gradient decided ahead of the randomness. hollow_intensity is the honest export: a slider for how much absence the form is permitted to contain.

botanical_flower.description: Standalone procedural flower — configurable petal count, length, width, curve, stem height, color hue, leaf count, and symmetry. A lightweight wrapper around the BotanicalFlower generator for map placement without VR controls.
botanical_flower.name: Botanical Flower

box_counting_dimension.description: Interactive box-counting dimension measurement on a Sierpinski triangle with log-log plot

branching_growth_algorithm.description: Interactive visualization of branching growth patterns and algorithmic plant generation
branching_growth_algorithm.name: Branching Growth Algorithm
branching_growth_algorithm.qfep_connection: Growth as a rule iterated — a tip that splits, angles, and splits again, each branch a smaller copy of the decision that made it. The engine behind the organic_space beside it: structure accumulating from a repeated local choice, the procedural chapter's handshake with the fractal one next door.

branching_growth_algorithm_continued.description: Continuous-growth variant — adds aging, energy decay, four growth phases, and attractor regeneration so the colonization runs as an ongoing ecosystem rather than a one-shot reach
branching_growth_algorithm_continued.name: Branching Growth Algorithm continued

cantor_set.description: cantor(bar) = [bar.left_third, bar.right_third], remove middle third, repeat. Measure → 0.
cantor_set.name: cantor_set

cave_explorer_3d_ui.name: cave_explorer_3d_ui
cave_explorer_3d_ui.qfep_connection: Inside Cave, Flat Landscape, Torus Sculpture, Dense Caves — five presets that are only parking spots in one continuous parameter space, and the sliders let you drive between them. The miniature proves the categories were never in the noise, only in where someone stopped scrolling.

cave_generator.description: Cellular automaton cave generation with flood-fill connectivity â€” classic roguelike technique. 64x64 grid initialized with random walls, smoothed by CA rules (5+ neighbors = wall), then flood-filled to keep only the largest connected region. Entrance and exit markers placed at region extremes.
cave_generator.name: Cave Generator

caverandomwalk.description: N walkers carve air from solid voxel grid — biased random walk inward, then upward level by level
caverandomwalk.name: caverandomwalk
caverandomwalk.qfep_connection: A cave dug by a random walk — a wanderer eating rock as it drifts, and the tunnel it leaves behind is the cave. The chapter's most direct marriage of the randomness thread and the space one: chance given a chisel, and the negative of its stagger becomes a place you can stand.

color_pattern_mate_texture_for_3d.description: Interactive 3D color pattern mate texture generation for procedural tiling
color_pattern_mate_texture_for_3d.name: Color Pattern Mate Texture for 3D
color_pattern_mate_texture_for_3d.qfep_connection: Random walks on an inner grid, doubled by a reflection rule, then bred: every tenth of a second the rows shift down and neighboring patterns mate into offspring. Ornament with a genetics — less a texture than a small population under glass.

color_pattern_texture_for_3d.description: Interactive 3D color pattern texture generation for procedural tiling systems
color_pattern_texture_for_3d.name: Color Pattern Texture for 3D

crackpropagation_ca.description: A cellular automaton that grows fracture networks from invisible stress. A 64x64 grid accumulates stress through diffusion and decay — when a cell crosses the crack threshold, it shatters and pushes stress outward. The result is realistic branching cracks that follow paths of least resistance, guided by direction bias that prevents zig-zag. You watch destruction emerge from accumulation: nothing visible happens until the threshold breaks, then cracks bloom explosively across the surface.
crackpropagation_ca.name: crackpropagation_ca
crackpropagation_ca.qfep_connection: Edge of chaos — the crack threshold is the critical lambda where order (intact material) meets entropy (shattered field). Below threshold: stability. Above: catastrophic branching. The propagation rate tunes how fast the phase transition sweeps through the grid.
crackpropagation_ca.gamwell_reference: Fracture mechanics, cellular automata, stress propagation, percolation theory, crack branching patterns in nature
interactions: watch cracks emerge from the center stress seed
observe branching patterns following direction bias
notice how crack width varies with local stress intensity
compare dense shatter (low threshold) vs sparse fractures (high threshold)
crackpropagation_ca.capacity: PREDICT how cellular automaton crack propagation creates realistic fracture networks from local stress transfer and threshold-based state transitions.

cube_bookshelf.description: Bookshelf created through cube subdivision - grid of shelves with frame and trim
cube_bookshelf.name: Cube Bookshelf

cube_cabin.description: Rustic cabin created through architectural cube subdivision - walls, door, windows, gabled roof, chimney and porch
cube_cabin.name: Cube Cabin

cube_chair.name: Cube Chair
cube_chair.qfep_connection: Eleven scaled boxes arrive at 0.3-second intervals — seat, back, four legs, armrests — and nothing else happens. Watching the schedule makes furniture legible as ordered proportions; non-uniform scaling is the only carpentry.

cube_desk.description: Modern desk with drawer unit created through cube subdivision
cube_desk.name: Cube Desk

cube_mound_scene.description: Procedural mound built from stacked cubes — layered cellular logic deposits cubes where conditions permit, producing terrain that is both built and eroded.
cube_mound_scene.name: cube_mound_scene
cube_mound_scene.qfep_connection: A mound built by stacked cubes under cellular logic — deposit a cube where the local conditions say yes, and a landform accretes with no landscaper. The chapter's plainest proof: give a rule a place to look and a thing to drop, and terrain grows itself, one conditional at a time.

cube_staircase.description: Staircase created through diagonal cube subdivision with treads, risers, stringers and handrail
cube_staircase.name: Cube Staircase

cube_subdivision.description: cube -> 8 sub-cubes -> pick one -> repeat. Scale reduction 0.5 per level.
cube_subdivision.name: cube_subdivision

dewcoveredfol.name: dewcoveredfol
dewcoveredfol.qfep_connection: Fifty leaf clusters, refractive droplets — then the reach: it instantiates its own sun and writes an Environment straight onto the viewport camera. A garden that annexes the weather; the dew never falls, but the morning light is compulsory.

dress_selector.description: Outfit selection interface with three mannequin display forms in Classic, Wicked, and Custom styles. Each mannequin has a selection button for choosing an outfit.
dress_selector.name: Dress Selector

example_8_3_recursion_circles_vr.description: circle(center, r, d) = torus(r) + 4 * circle(center +/- offset, r * 0.5, d-1)
example_8_3_recursion_circles_vr.name: example_8_3_recursion_circles_vr

example_8_4_cantor_pagoda_vr.description: Cantor Pagoda - 3D extension of Cantor set principle
example_8_4_cantor_pagoda_vr.name: example_8_4_cantor_pagoda_vr

example_8_4_cantor_set_vr.description: Cantor Set - infinite subdivision creating zero measure infinite set
example_8_4_cantor_set_vr.name: example_8_4_cantor_set_vr

example_8_6_recursive_tree_vr.name: example_8_6_recursive_tree_vr
example_8_6_recursive_tree_vr.qfep_connection: Shiffman's branching rule carried into VR with exactly one degree of freedom handed to the body: a graspable angle between 10 and 60 degrees. Move it and the whole tree is deleted and re-derived — the angle is not an adjustment but the tree's entire genome.

fabrics.name: fabrics
fabrics.qfep_connection: Wallpaper, stone, terrain, tartan — one turbulence trick wearing different costumes across planes and boxes, the same shader reparametrized from wall covering to landscape. Cloth here is a claim made by three floats; materials are positions in parameter space, not substances.

fatwireframe.description: Procedural wireframe generation with adjustable line thickness and geometric complexity
fatwireframe.name: Fat Wireframe
fatwireframe.qfep_connection: Faces are discarded and only edges survive, their thickness faked from barycentric distance in the fragment shader. A debug convention promoted to matter: the wireframe was always the diagram under the surface, here it is granted glow and bulk and asked to stand as the thing itself.

fibonacci_pagoda.description: tier_scale(n) = base_scale / phi^(n*0.5), stacking Fibonacci-ratioed tiers with golden finial
fibonacci_pagoda.name: fibonacci_pagoda

fibonacci_terrain.description: Terrain generated through golden ratio subdivision - plane subdivides, random non-edge faces lift and subdivide. Presets: gentle_hills, mountain_peak, plateau, archipelago, fibonacci_spiral
fibonacci_terrain.name: Fibonacci Terrain

flower_lab.description: Interactive botanical laboratory â€” VR sliders control petal count, length, width, curve, stem height, color hue, leaf count, and symmetry of a procedural BotanicalFlower. Randomize to discover unexpected morphologies, save presets to JSON. Teaches how parametric variation drives flower form.
flower_lab.name: Flower Lab

fractal_cantor_set.description: Classic Cantor set fractal demonstrating infinite subdivision
fractal_cantor_set.name: Cantor Set

fractal_clouds.description: Volumetric clouds using fractal Brownian motion noise. Presets: cumulus, stratus, cirrus, storm
fractal_clouds.name: Fractal Clouds

fractal_koch_curve.description: Koch snowflake curve fractal with recursive edge patterns
fractal_koch_curve.name: Koch Curve

fractal_lsystem_tree.description: L-System tree generation with formal grammar rules
fractal_lsystem_tree.name: L-System Tree
fractal_lsystem_tree.qfep_connection: The bridge to the next chapter grown early: a tree written as grammar, branches as rewrite rules. Standing among the recursive trees it whispers that recursion and language are the same machine.

fractal_recursion_1.description: Basic recursion visualization demonstrating fundamental recursive patterns
fractal_recursion_1.name: Fractal Recursion 1
fractal_recursion_1.qfep_connection: The primitive laid bare: a shape calling itself, depth one, two, three — recursion slowed down until you can watch the stack breathe.

fractal_recursion_2.description: Advanced recursion patterns with multiple levels of depth
fractal_recursion_2.name: Fractal Recursion 2
fractal_recursion_2.qfep_connection: The same breath at depth: multiple recursive levels interleaving until the pattern stops reading as repetition and starts reading as texture — the moment quantity of recursion becomes quality of surface.

fractal_recursion_circles.description: Circular recursive fractal patterns demonstrating self-similarity
fractal_recursion_circles.name: Recursive Circles

fractal_recursive_tree.description: Branching tree structure using recursive algorithms
fractal_recursive_tree.name: Recursive Tree
fractal_recursive_tree.qfep_connection: Growth staged as re-execution: each animation level clears every branch and reruns the recursion one depth deeper. Nothing accumulates; the tree has no past, only a function called with a larger argument — development impersonated by recomputation.

fractal_scene.name: fractal_scene
fractal_scene.qfep_connection: A composed fractal tableau — the chapter's specimens arranged as one scene, self-similarity as scenography.

fractal_stochastic_tree.description: Randomized recursive tree with natural variation
fractal_stochastic_tree.name: Stochastic Tree
fractal_stochastic_tree.qfep_connection: The recursive tree with dice in its grammar: every branch angle and length drawn from a distribution. Same rule, different tree each run — the fractal chapter shaking hands with the randomness chapter, determinism loosened just enough to look alive.

genetic_programming.description: Genetic programming interface for evolving 3D shapes â€” populations of genomes (Primitives, CSG Trees, Parametric, Voxel, L-Systems) undergo selection, crossover, and mutation toward fitness goals like target volume, height, and symmetry. Visualizes the entire population in a grid with real-time evolution.
genetic_programming.name: Genetic Programming

glassdivider.name: glassdivider
glassdivider.qfep_connection: Three freestanding partitions — stand, panel, frosted-glass shader — the cubicle's minimal unit, tripled. Frost is order applied to sight alone: the panel stops no body, only detail, keeping the person beyond it present enough to be monitored and blurred enough to be denied — the office's actual proposal, adjacency without particulars.

golden_rectangle.description: Classic golden ratio rectangle subdivision with Fibonacci spiral. Shows numbers 1,1,2,3,5,8,13,21... Presets: classic, minimal, rainbow, deep, fast
golden_rectangle.name: Golden Rectangle

gridscheckers.name: gridscheckers
gridscheckers.qfep_connection: Checkers, line grids, diagonal stripes, an Albers nod — modernism's flat pattern vocabulary redone as a few step functions and a UV scale per box. F_order at its cheapest: the shader supplies thresholds and the eye volunteers the loom.

ik_arm_demo.description: Standalone TwoBoneIK3D arm demonstration — two procedural arms with animated targets tracing figure-8 patterns. Shows the same inverse kinematics solver used for VR body tracking.
ik_arm_demo.name: IK Arm Demo

implicit_surface_modeling.description: Metaball-based implicit surface generation and modeling
implicit_surface_modeling.name: Implicit Surface Modeling
implicit_surface_modeling.qfep_connection: The closing craft: modeling by writing functions — union as min, intersection as max, blending as soft algebra. Shape as sentence: say the field precisely enough and the surface is the proof.

inverted_tree_cloud.description: tree(depth) = trunk_down + branches_down(random_angle, shrink) + cube_cloud(orbit, fade_timeline)
inverted_tree_cloud.name: inverted_tree_cloud

julia_set.description: Complex plane fractal visualization of Julia sets
julia_set.name: Julia Set
julia_set.qfep_connection: One c, one temperament: where Mandelbrot maps the whole family, a Julia set is a single member's portrait — connected dust or lace depending on which c you chose. The pair teaches the deepest grammar in the chapter: parameter space and behavior space are different rooms, and beauty lives at their border.

koch_curve_3d.description: Three-dimensional recursive Koch snowflake curve generation
koch_curve_3d.name: 3D Koch Curve

layered_membrane.description: Procedural membrane generation with layered structures
layered_membrane.name: Layered Membrane
layered_membrane.qfep_connection: Surfaces accreted in layers, each draping over the last — sediment, skin, stratum. Form as history made visible: the membrane is a record of the order in which its rule fired, procedural generation wearing its own timeline.

liquid_simulation.description: Particle-based liquid simulation and fluid dynamics
liquid_simulation.name: Liquid Simulation
liquid_simulation.qfep_connection: Water, oil and honey diffuse while a floating label reports the Shannon entropy of the mix — but the normalising ceiling is hard-coded for two species at 50/50, so three liquids can overflow the scale built to measure them. Irreversibility, metered by an instrument that undercounts it.

mandelbrot_set.description: Fractal visualization of the famous Mandelbrot set
mandelbrot_set.name: Mandelbrot Set
mandelbrot_set.qfep_connection: The world's most famous boundary: for each point c, iterate z squared plus c and ask if it stays home. The set is the atlas of every Julia set at once — an infinitely deep coastline grown from one line of arithmetic. The chapter's proof that the simplest sentence can contain a world that no one, including its discoverer, has finished visiting.

marching_cubes_cave_gallery.name: marching_cubes_cave_gallery
marching_cubes_cave_gallery.qfep_connection: Human, chair, house, bottle, cup, computer — six everyday nouns rewritten as signed-distance fields and pushed through one mesher at body scale. The levelling is the point: under the isosurface regime a person and their furniture are the same kind of object, the zero-set of a function.

marching_cubes_gallery.name: marching_cubes_gallery
marching_cubes_gallery.qfep_connection: Filed in the WFC sculpture folder, but the script it loads is the marching-cubes gallery, with trace_individual_elements splitting each result into connected components. A room whose name outlived its mechanism — what it actually stages is the mesher's habit of shedding islands, promoted here to curatorial method.

marching_cubes_sculpt_vr.description: VR paintable marching cubes - sculpt in 3D with your controllers using GPU compute shaders
marching_cubes_sculpt_vr.name: Marching Cubes VR Sculpt
marching_cubes_sculpt_vr.qfep_connection: Both triggers write density straight into a 64-cubed field and the isosurface chases your hands at frame rate; erase mode is the same brush with the sign reversed. The algorithm that elsewhere authors whole terrains is here demoted to rendering intent — matter and void as one channel a body can scribble in.

marchingcave.name: marchingcave
marchingcave.qfep_connection: A cave system marched at generation scale — the algorithm as land-maker, corridors and chambers emerging wherever the noise dips below the line.

marchingcubes_cave.name: marchingcubes_cave
marchingcubes_cave.qfep_connection: The cave generator opened as an instrument: field in, fifteen cases per cell, mesh out. The pipeline of the whole chapter run end to end while you watch.

marchingcubes_flat_landscape.name: marchingcubes_flat_landscape
marchingcubes_flat_landscape.qfep_connection: The threshold sits at 0.05 where the cave variant holds 0.88 — landscape and cavern are the same density field read at different iso-levels, ground and rock separated by one float. When the compute shader fails, sine-summed hills quietly stand in, and the ontology swap goes unnoticed.

marchingcubes_inside_cave.name: marchingcubes_inside_cave
marchingcubes_inside_cave.qfep_connection: The fallback tunnel manufactures interiority with a sign flip — every normal pointed inward — while the compute path earns it by raising the iso-level until void outnumbers rock. Being enclosed is something the mesh asserts, not somewhere you are.

marchingcubes_portal_landscape.name: marchingcubes_portal_landscape
marchingcubes_portal_landscape.qfep_connection: A landscape with a portal, marched from a scalar field — threshold as terrain and doorway at once. The level-set that decides where stone becomes air also decides where a passage opens, so the same number that shapes the ground carves the way through it. The field as both floor and gate.

marchingcubes_torus_sculpture.name: marchingcubes_torus_sculpture
marchingcubes_torus_sculpture.qfep_connection: The compute shader carves its torus out of a density field; the fallback just calls TorusMesh.new(). Same genus, opposite politics — one earns the hole, the other declares it.

maze_generation.description: VR-scale walkable maze with recursive backtracking generation
maze_generation.name: Maze Generation
maze_generation.qfep_connection: A walkable maze carved by recursive backtracking — the algorithm drills forward at random, and when it hits a dead end it reverses just far enough to try a new direction, until every cell has been visited exactly once. The result is a perfect maze, one path between any two points, and no designer ever saw the whole of it. Getting lost in a corridor no mind laid out.

maze_generator.description: Procedural maze generation â€” watch walls carve out paths through depth-first search, recursive backtracking, or randomized algorithms. Every maze is a spanning tree of a grid graph.
maze_generator.name: Maze Generator

menger_sponge.description: menger(cube) = 20 * menger(sub-cubes at kept positions), remove 7 cross-cubes per iteration. D = log(20)/log(3) ~ 2.727.
menger_sponge.name: menger_sponge

metaballs.description: Interactive metaball visualization demonstrating implicit surface modeling
metaballs.name: Metaballs

mirror_artifact.description: Reflective mirror panel showing the player what their hands look like. A large vertical mirror surface with metallic material and decorative wooden frame.
mirror_artifact.name: Mirror Artifact

mirror_cellular_texture_for_3d.description: Interactive 3D cellular automata with mirroring and texture generation capabilities
mirror_cellular_texture_for_3d.name: Mirror Cellular Texture for 3D
mirror_cellular_texture_for_3d.qfep_connection: Cellular automata run and then mirrored — local disorder folded across an axis into pattern with a spine. The room's demonstration that symmetry is cheap: take any grown texture, reflect it, and the eye reads intention where there was only a rule and a fold.

modelsynthesis.description: Model Synthesis (Merrell 2007) — 3D voxel generation via overlap constraints from exemplar with coherence search
modelsynthesis.name: modelsynthesis

modernistchairgallery.description: Physics constraint systems for maintaining object relationships
modernistchairgallery.name: modernistchairgallery
modernistchairgallery.qfep_connection: Breuer, Mies, Eames, Bertoia — a canon reduced to ten constructors instantiated in a circle, every chair rotated to face a center where no sitter ever arrives. Design history survives here exactly as far as it can be rewritten as a class hierarchy with a Label3D for provenance.

mushrooms.description: A procedural mushroom meadow grown from noise. FastNoiseLite drives a spatial Poisson process — mushrooms spawn where noise exceeds a density threshold, creating natural clearings and clusters. Five species templates produce variety; a glowing variant adds bioluminescent accents. Fairy rings self-organize as perfect circles of identical species within the random field. The ground itself is procedurally deformed, and ambient lighting creates a forest-floor atmosphere. Walk through and feel how randomness filtered through ecological rules produces something that looks alive.
mushrooms.name: Mushrooms
mushrooms.qfep_connection: E(S) entropy filtered through ecological form — noise is the raw entropy, density threshold is the filter, and species templates are the forms that entropy fills. Fairy rings are emergent order: lambda-tuning where structured patterns crystallize from random placement.
mushrooms.gamwell_reference: Spatial Poisson processes, noise-driven procedural generation, fairy ring mycology, bioluminescent fungi, ecological niche theory
interactions: find fairy rings — perfect circles of identical species
spot glowing mushrooms in the undergrowth
notice how clearings form from noise thresholds
mushrooms.capacity: EXPLAIN how noise-driven spatial processes create naturalistic distributions and how fairy rings emerge as self-organized order within random fields.

necklace_anchor.description: Pendant necklace display on a stand showing the concept of an identity anchor point. A vertical stand with torus ring, glowing gem pendant that slowly rotates.
necklace_anchor.name: Necklace Anchor

penteract_double_projection.description: 5D hypercube (penteract) projected twice â€” from 5D to 4D to 3D. The shadow of a shadow of a higher-dimensional object, revealing structure invisible from any single viewpoint.
penteract_double_projection.name: Penteract Double Projection
penteract_double_projection.qfep_connection: Thirty-two vertices, an edge wherever two indices differ by one bit, then two flattenings in a row before anything is drawable. What orbits in front of you is a compression of a compression, recomputed every frame — the penteract never arrives, only its loss schedule.

percolationnetwork_ca.description: P(occupied) = threshold -> CA flow propagation from top to bottom — does the random lattice percolate?
percolationnetwork_ca.name: percolationnetwork_ca
percolationnetwork_ca.qfep_connection: Percolation: raise the density of open cells and, at one sharp threshold, disconnected pockets suddenly span the whole space — a path appears from edge to edge where an instant before there was none. The turn's physics: connectivity is not gradual, it is a phase change, and the procedural world snaps from rubble to network at a single critical value. Where forests burn, fluids seep, and rumors spread.

reaction_diffusion.description: Turing pattern generation using reaction-diffusion systems â€” the Gray-Scott model on a 2D grid producing spots, stripes, and labyrinthine patterns from two interacting chemicals.
reaction_diffusion.name: Reaction Diffusion

reaction_diffusion_vr.description: Turing reaction-diffusion patterns in VR â€” two chemicals activating and inhibiting each other, producing spots, stripes, and labyrinthine patterns. The math behind animal markings.
reaction_diffusion_vr.name: Reaction Diffusion (VR)

recursive_boolean_cube.description: menger(center, size, d) = {subcube(i) for i in 27 if zeros(i) < 2}, recursive cross-removal
recursive_boolean_cube.name: recursive_boolean_cube

recursive_chair.description: Chair created through recursive cube subdivision
recursive_chair.name: Recursive Chair

recursive_table.description: table = subdivide_3x2(cube) -> keep(top_layer, corner_legs) -> flatten(top) -> stretch(legs)
recursive_table.name: recursive_table

recursive_tree.description: branch(pos, dir, len, depth) = cylinder(tapered) + branch_count * branch(end, rotated_dir, len * 0.7, depth+1)
recursive_tree.name: recursive_tree

recursive_tree_2.name: recursive_tree_2
recursive_tree_2.qfep_connection: A second recursive tree at different proportions — the same rule wearing another body, which is the chapter's definition of a family.

romanesco.description: romanesco(cone, depth) = 13 * romanesco(cone * 0.382, depth+1) placed at 137.508 degree golden angle intervals
romanesco.name: romanesco

room_grammar.description: Shape grammar for architectural floor plans â€” binary space partitioning recursively splits a rectangle into rooms, draws wall outlines, adds door gaps, and colors rooms by area. The algorithmic foundation behind roguelike dungeon generation.
room_grammar.name: Room Grammar

sierpinski_triangle.description: sierpinski(v1,v2,v3,d) = 3 * sierpinski(corners, midpoints, d+1), skip center triangle. D = log(3)/log(2) ~ 1.585.
sierpinski_triangle.name: sierpinski_triangle

slime_mold.description: Interactive slime mold simulation using Dave Stewart's tube algorithm
slime_mold.name: Slime Mold
slime_mold.qfep_connection: Pools as nodes, tubes as commitments, a viscosity float doing the deciding: infrastructure without an engineer, after Physarum. But the network is sculpted, not grown — a still life of an optimization, holding the pose of intelligence the organism actually performs.

space_colonization_algorithm.description: Growth algorithm that builds branching structures by attracting tips toward a cloud of auxin-like markers — Runions-style space colonisation producing tree/coral/blood-vessel topologies.
space_colonization_algorithm.name: space_colonization_algorithm
space_colonization_algorithm.qfep_connection: The algorithm that grows a tree the way a tree grows: scatter invisible attractors (auxin, the growth hormone), and let branch tips crawl toward the nearest ones, consuming them as they arrive. No blueprint of the tree exists anywhere — the form is the negotiation between hungry tips and a cloud of demand. Venation, antlers, river deltas, lightning: all this one rule, met with different clouds.

spherenetwork.name: spherenetwork
spherenetwork.qfep_connection: Habitable space made purely by subtraction: CSG carves walkway bores out of solid spheres and the pipes between them, so everywhere you could stand is exactly where material was revoked. Architecture as negative accounting — the corridor is the deficit.

stochastic_tree_separated.name: stochastic_tree_separated
stochastic_tree_separated.qfep_connection: The stochastic tree with its variation pulled apart for inspection — rule and randomness shown as separable ingredients, so the eye can credit each with what it actually contributes.

terrain_erosion.description: Hydraulic erosion on a procedural heightmap â€” layered sin-wave terrain eroded by 800 virtual water droplets flowing downhill, carrying and depositing sediment. ImmediateMesh surface colored by altitude: water, beach, grass, rock, snow.
terrain_erosion.name: Terrain Erosion
terrain_erosion.qfep_connection: Eight hundred droplets rewrite a heightmap that admits, in its own comment, to being layered sines impersonating Perlin — and the RNG is pinned to seed 42, so every visitor inherits the identical island with the identical scars. Erosion as history, but a history that already happened, once, for everyone.

tesseract_net_space_showcase.name: tesseract_net_space_showcase
tesseract_net_space_showcase.qfep_connection: A tesseract can only visit 3-space unfolded, so the room is bricked from its nets — Dalí crosses rotated and offset like masonry, the center deliberately left hollow. You stand inside an absence framed by flattened higher dimension; the fourth axis appears only as the fold that never happens.

tesseract_tunnel.description: Fly through a tunnel of rotating tesseracts â€” 4D hypercubes projected into 3D, their inner and outer cubes visible simultaneously. Experience the shadow of a higher dimension.
tesseract_tunnel.name: Tesseract Tunnel

test_scene_5.name: test
test_scene_5.qfep_connection: The description still reads 'this is the test' while the scene grows the finished recursive tree. Scaffolding promoted to content without renaming: place the token in a map and a whole tree rises under a label that confesses it was never meant to stay — the registry's dark spot, walkable.

tile_patterns.description: Procedural tile pattern generation and tiling algorithms
tile_patterns.name: Tile Patterns

torso_estimation_vis.description: 3-point torso estimation demo — shows how head + two hand positions estimate torso orientation. Animated tracking points with visible shoulder computation and forward direction.
torso_estimation_vis.name: Torso Estimation Visualization

tree_gen.description: An infinite procedural forest that grows around you. Trees spawn within a generation radius as you walk, and vanish behind you when you leave. The generation loop is the algorithm: proximity check, spacing constraint, spawn, cull. No tree exists until you approach; the forest is an illusion maintained by continuous generation. Two tree styles (simple blocks and complex clusters) with red emissive materials create an alien forest that feels both procedural and alive.
tree_gen.name: Tree Generator
tree_gen.qfep_connection: Pure phi — the rate of change IS the content. The forest exists only as a process of generation and removal. Stop walking and the forest freezes. The generation_distance parameter controls how far ahead reality extends.
tree_gen.gamwell_reference: Procedural world generation, infinite terrain, proximity-based LOD, parametric tree generation, spatial hashing
interactions: walk forward to generate new trees ahead
look behind to see trees vanishing at removal distance
observe two tree styles appearing randomly
tree_gen.capacity: BUILD a proximity-based procedural spawning system that creates and destroys content around the player position to simulate infinite generated worlds.

truchettiles.name: truchettiles
truchettiles.qfep_connection: One floor cut into four quadrants, each running a different fragment shader — quarter-arcs, diagonal split, dots, zigzag — with a sample solid hovering above wearing the same program. The quarter-arc corner states the Truchet bargain plainly: a single tile plus one orientation bit per cell is enough to produce unbounded corridor, pattern as the cheapest possible seed.

voronoi_diagrams.description: Spatial partitioning using Voronoi tessellation algorithms
voronoi_diagrams.name: Voronoi Diagrams
voronoi_diagrams.qfep_connection: The seeds are real but the instruments are theatre: uniformity_score is elapsed time times 0.85, coverage times 0.9, climbing regardless of what the cells do. A lesson in partitioning space wearing a scoreboard that measures nothing but duration.

water_flowers.description: Floating flowers on physically simulated Gerstner waves — buoyancy, wave alignment, and drift create a mesmerizing water garden. Configurable flower count, water size, wave strength, and drift speed.
water_flowers.name: Water Flowers

wave_function_collapse.description: Procedural generation using wave function collapse algorithm
wave_function_collapse.name: Wave Function Collapse
wave_function_collapse.qfep_connection: Each cell wears its entropy as a floating number and its possible futures as mini-tiles, and collapse always picks on whoever has the fewest options left. Certainty spreads not by decree but by neighbors deleting each other's possibilities — constraint propagation slowed to watching speed.

waves.name: waves
waves.qfep_connection: Water as the sum of its tells: noise textures for swell, a normal map for glitter, Beer's-law fade for depth, edge foam for shore — four quads, none of them wet. Convincingness assembled from parts, each shader a different bet on which cue the body will believe.

wfc.description: Wave Function Collapse algorithm â€” generating complex patterns from local adjacency constraints. Start with superposition of all possibilities, observe one tile, propagate constraints until the world resolves.
wfc.name: Wave Function Collapse
wfc.qfep_connection: Every cell begins holding all tiles at once, and the world exists only as options are deleted — collapse leaves a single survivor and propagation prunes the neighbours. Compatibility is nothing deeper than one edge-string equalling another reversed: global coherence rented entirely from local string-matching.

rd_coral_garden.name: Gray-Scott Coral Garden
rd_coral_garden.description: Walkable polyp forest grown from Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion. Two constants (F, K) — no designer placed the pillars, the rule did. Uses the commons/rd_grammar substrate from the DNA research loop.

gray_scott_comparison.name: Gray-Scott Comparison Garden
gray_scott_comparison.description: Nine mini-gardens arranged 3×3, each running the same reaction-diffusion equations with a different (F, K) preset. Walking between them teaches the thesis directly: same equations, different constants, different ecology. The pedagogical punchline of pattern formation.

seed_orb.name: Seed Orb
seed_orb.description: The new λ_edge affordance for proceduralgeneration. Player throws a glowing seed; where it lands, procedural growth happens around it. Terrain bumps, tile constraints, L-system-like branches. The seed is input, the world is output — an author isn't needed for a world.

registry_info.description: Additional procedural generation artifacts â€” wave function collapse, higher-dimensional polytopes, reaction diffusion, and maze generation. The constructive side of algorithms.
registry_info.name: procgen_extra
registry_info.theoretical_grounding: Constraint satisfaction (WFC), higher-dimensional geometry (tesseracts, penteracts), Turing patterns, maze generation algorithms
